one_month_reasoning: Events in the window to 2026-11-12: (1) lock-up supply. Staged early releases of ~19.4M shares on Oct 14 and Oct 28, then the final expiry of all remaining locked shares on Nov 9 (or 2 trading days after Q3 results, if earlier). Source: the Motley Fool lock-up schedule, built from the prospectus terms. Officers are already selling: a Form 144 on 2026-09-29 covered 396k shares (~$78M), and venture holder Eclipse distributed its shares in kind in August (13D/A). The schedule is public and the stock is already -52% from its first close and below the $185 IPO price, so this should be largely priced in. I expect a small negative drift, not a collapse. (2) Q3 2026 results: no date announced and no 8-K since Aug 12. Q2 came 43 days after quarter-end, which points to about Nov 10-12, likely after the close, so there is probably less than a 40% chance the print lands in the window. The company guided Q3 core revenue $214-216M, core GM 38-40%, core operating margin -25% to -23%. It beat its own Q2 guide, but the stock fell after that print anyway. (3) The unconfirmed early-October report (SemiAnalysis on X, relayed by press) that OpenAI's 'Ultrafast' mode moved to Nvidia GPUs, which OpenAI's CEO softened publicly. It is sentiment, not a cancellation: the 10-Q says OpenAI is contractually committed to the 750MW Committed Capacity. Net: median ~$146.5 (slightly below spot for lock-up supply and negative momentum, partly offset by short-term reversal after a -20% week). Spread is a lognormal sigma of 0.26 for the month (~90% annualised: below the 115% realised IPO-period vol, above the base annual/3.5 because of the possible earnings print and the unlock dates).

fair_value.method: Blend of a 5-year DCF (WACC 14.8% from a 2.29 comparable beta, exit 14x FY2030 GAAP EBITDA) and 7.0x NTM EV/sales at the horizon on ~$5.2B NTM core revenue, plus ~$4B net cash at the horizon, over 298.4M fully diluted shares (all warrants, RSUs and most options included).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Core revenue $885M FY26 -> $2.95B FY27 -> $6.0B FY28 -> $7.4B FY29 -> $8.3B FY30; GAAP EBIT margin -85%/-8%/12%/18%/22%; capex 160%/80%/30%/18%/15% of revenue; WACC 14.8%; exit 14x FY2030 EBITDA (~$3.0B); net cash $7.0B at 2026-06-30 less burn; 298.4M shares.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2025 total revenue from the 424B4 summary financial data; core revenue FY2025 is about the same (FY2026 original core guide $855-865M was stated as +69% at the midpoint, i.e. ~$509M base).
Midpoint of raised FY2026 core revenue guidance $880-890M (Q2 release) / $510M - 1 = 73.5%. Consensus FY2026 revenue $887.1M agrees.
Consensus FY2027 revenue $2.95B (11 analysts) / $885M - 1 = 233%; consistent with the CFO's statement in the Q2 release that the company plans to 'more than triple revenue in 2027'.

RPO $25.4B at 2026-06-30, ~22% ($5.6B) to be recognized by 2028-06-30 and 43% ($10.9B, ~$5.5B a year) in months 25-48 (10-Q). Backing out ~$2.1B of 2027 OpenAI revenue (consensus $2.95B less ~$0.8B non-OpenAI) leaves ~$3.2B for H1 2028; H2 2028 at the ~$5.5B/yr months-25-48 pace adds ~$2.7B, so OpenAI-related ~$5.5-6B in 2028, plus ~$0.5-1B other customers, haircut for deployment slippage -> $6.0B.

Months 25-48 of RPO run at ~$5.5B a year (10-Q schedule), so contracted revenue plateaus; growth after 2028 comes from other cloud/API customers and OpenAI's 1.25GW additional-capacity option (not in the base).

FY26: core operating margin guide -19% to -17% (Q2 release) less SBC of ~67% of revenue (H1 SBC $386.6M incl. $273.6M IPO RSU catch-up, plus ~$105M a quarter ongoing). FY27: consensus non-GAAP EPS $1.27 x ~300M shares = ~$0.38B, less ~$0.25B interest income on cash -> ~5% non-GAAP operating margin, less SBC ~14% of revenue -> -8%. FY28-30: core gross margin 41-43% guided for FY26 rising with scale; operating leverage on R&D -> core 20-28%, less SBC 6-8%.
Loss-making with accumulated losses (FY2024 net loss $481.6M, FY2026 H1 operating loss $492.3M per filings) so cash taxes stay low as NOLs are used.

H1 2026 depreciation $42.6M on revenue $373.5M = 11% (XBRL); construction in progress $604.0M and capex $548.9M in H1 put the owned capacity build on the balance sheet, so D&A rises as it goes into service.

H1 2026 capex $548.9M on revenue $373.5M (147%); continuing the build-out for the 750MW OpenAI committed capacity and 600MW+ live or contracted by end-2027 (Q2 release) -> ~$1.4B FY26, ~$2.4B FY27, then tapering to maintenance plus growth. No company capex guidance is published.
Prepaid and other assets rose $182.3M in H1 2026 (XBRL); capacity contracts are partly prepaid by the customer (OpenAI working-capital loan), so a modest 10%.
FY2026 H1 SBC $386.6M; Q2 ongoing SBC excluding the $273.6M catch-up ~$103M a quarter; held at ~$0.4B in 2027 and grown slower than revenue after. Costed in EBIT (GAAP basis).

Cost of equity = 5.24% (10-year Treasury 2026-10-09) + 2.29 (median 2-year beta of NVDA, AMD, AVGO, ALAB, CRDO, CRWV, NBIS from the brief note) x 4.20% (Damodaran implied ERP 2026-10-01) = 14.9%. Debt is the $918M OpenAI working-capital loan at 6% (10-Q), ~2% of capital and repayable in kind -> WACC ~14.8%. No relevering: Cerebras and most peers hold net cash.

NVDA trades at 27.2x TTM EV/EBITDA (NVDA.ev_ebitda_ttm) and CRWV at 23.5x (StockAnalysis). 14x is a deep discount for maturing growth (~12% in 2030) and the risk that the OpenAI MRA (3-4 year term, extendable to 5 per the 10-Q) is not renewed on the same terms around 2030-31.

Cash $6,742.2M (F1) + short-term investments $1,179.4M (F2) - debt $918.2M (F3+F4: the OpenAI working-capital loan). Restricted cash $0.68B and the undrawn $850M revolver are excluded. Lease liabilities ($568.8M) are left out because lease cost is already in EBIT.

237.56M common shares outstanding on 2026-08-05 (10-Q cover) + 16.53M unvested RSUs + ~20.0M of 23.80M options (treasury-method allowance, strikes not disclosed) + 23.41M unvested OpenAI warrant shares (33,445,026 less 4,459,337 and 5,574,171 vested) + 0.89M AWS warrant at $100 strike (2.70M x (1-100/149)). 9.0M PRSUs are excluded as contingent. No buybacks; SBC is costed in EBIT, so the count is held flat.

Peer CY2027 EV/sales median 10.0x (range 3.3-32.7x). Neoclouds CRWV 3.4x and NBIS 4.75x (mean ~4.1x); AI silicon NVDA/AMD/AVGO/MRVL/ALAB/CRDO median ~10.4x. Cerebras's 2027+ revenue is mostly capacity sold as a service on its own hardware (cloud 70% of Q2 revenue). A 70/30 blend gives ~6.1x; +0.9 turn for own-silicon gross margin and faster NTM growth -> 7.0x, inside the range and below the median for low GAAP margins and OpenAI concentration.

bear.story: OpenAI moves incremental fast-inference work to GPU/ASIC platforms and Cerebras's capacity ramp slips (datacenter or next-gen product transition), so revenue grows ~20 points a year slower, margins stay ~6 points lower, and the market values it like a neocloud at ~4x NTM sales.

base.story: FY2027 revenue ~$2.95B (consensus, CFO 'more than triple'), FY2028 ~$6B as the 750MW OpenAI committed capacity is delivered on the RPO schedule; GAAP EBIT turns positive in 2028; 7x NTM EV/sales at the horizon.

bull.story: OpenAI exercises part of its 1.25GW additional-capacity option, AWS Bedrock (Q1 2027) and AMD disaggregated inference add non-OpenAI demand, core gross margin expands, and the stock re-rates to ~11x NTM sales, near the AI-silicon median.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward (fiscal year covering most of CY2027) P/E 13.0x-82.7x across 9 profitable peers (median 36.4x; CRWV, NBIS n/m). EV/sales 3.3x-32.7x across 11 peers (median 10.0x; ARM and ORCL on P/S because the filings tags give no EV). Forward EV/EBITDA consensus was not reachable: the Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate/statistics endpoints are premium, and StockAnalysis gives revenue/EPS only. Filing-based TTM EV/EBITDA exists only for NVDA (27.2x, NVDA.ev_ebitda_ttm). So the peer median EV/EBITDA is left null rather than guessed.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 7.0x NTM EV/sales at the horizon, 3 turns below the 10.0x median and inside the 3.3-32.7x range. It sits between the neocloud pair (CRWV 3.4x, NBIS 4.75x) and the AI-silicon group (NVDA 7.9x, CRDO 9.3x, AVGO 10.0x, AMD 10.8x, MRVL 11.9x, ALAB 18.1x). P/E is not used: Cerebras has negative GAAP EPS through 2027 and consensus FY2027 non-GAAP EPS is only $1.27.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount to the median for four reasons that should persist through the horizon. (1) Business mix: cloud and other services were 70% of Q2 2026 revenue ($126.0M of $180.1M), and the OpenAI MRA is a capacity contract delivered from Cerebras-funded systems (H1 2026 capex $548.9M, CIP $604.0M). Economically that is closer to a neocloud than to a fabless chip vendor. (2) Margins: FY2026 core gross margin guide is 41-43% and core operating margin -19% to -17%, against 30-60% operating margins at the silicon peers. (3) Concentration: one customer was 34% and OpenAI 32% of Q2 revenue, and most of the $25.4B RPO is OpenAI. (4) GAAP noise: $44.3M of Q2 warrant amortization was booked as contra-revenue. Partial offset (why it is above the neocloud pair): own silicon, so no third-party GPU margin to pay, and faster NTM growth at the horizon (~+100% vs ~60% for the peers).

thesis_break_reason: At $85 the equity is ~$25B, or EV ~$21B on ~$4B net cash at the horizon. That is ~4x NTM sales, the neocloud multiple. It would most likely mean the market has decided one of three things: (a) the OpenAI 750MW commitment is being delivered late or renegotiated (watch RPO, warrant vesting milestones and 'Committed Capacity' language in the 10-Qs); (b) wafer-scale inference has lost its speed edge to GPU/ASIC systems (more workload-loss reports like the October 'Ultrafast' one, confirmed by OpenAI or by falling non-OpenAI cloud revenue); or (c) the capacity build needs outside capital before positive FCF. $85 is ~43% below spot and below the bear-weighted 25th percentile of my distribution, so it is past ordinary IPO-period volatility.

key_uncertainties: OpenAI dependence: OpenAI was ~32% of Q2 revenue ($56.8M) and most of the $25.4B RPO. The October report of a workload moving to Nvidia is unconfirmed, but it shows the binding contract may not grow beyond the 750MW committed.

Execution of the capacity build: Q2 GAAP gross margin fell to 14% ($11.8M E&O inventory charges for the next-gen transition, depreciation in cost of revenue up to $18.5M). Delays push the RPO-implied ramp (22% of RPO by mid-2028) to the right.
Cash needs: H1 2026 operating cash flow -$47.5M and capex $548.9M. $8.6B of liquidity plus the $850M revolver should fund 2027, but heavier capex for the 1.25GW option would need outside capital.
The core vs GAAP gap (pass-through revenue, warrant contra-revenue of $44.3M in Q2, SBC $377M in Q2) makes headline GAAP figures look far worse than core figures and can unsettle holders.
Supply overhang through Nov 9 and continued insider and VC distributions after it.
UAE customer and export-control exposure: G42 and MBZUAI were 86% of FY2025 revenue.

reverse_dcf_check: The engine says the 7.0x NTM EV/sales leg ($138) would equal my DCF cash flows only at a ~5.1% WACC, far below the 14.8% CAPM rate. Put another way: at 14.8%, matching $138 needs a FY2030 exit of ~19.3x GAAP EBITDA instead of my 14x. I tested this: 18x gives $130 and 20x gives $143. That is ~7x FY2030 sales for a business then growing ~12%, with ~22% GAAP EBIT and ~36% EBITDA margins, and it would have to persist through the OpenAI renewal around 2030-31. Holding the margins, it amounts to assuming growth stays above 15-20% well past 2030 or margins reach the high-20s/30% EBIT. That is possible if wafer-scale inference keeps a speed edge and OpenAI renews or expands (bull case). It is not my base case given the post-horizon renewal and competition risks in long_dated_risks. So the multiple leg is the optimistic leg and the DCF ($104 at 14x exit) the conservative one. The 60/40 blend at $124.76 embeds probability-weighted long-dated risk effects of about -$17/share.

sbc_treatment.note: FY2025 SBC was $49.8M (424B4). FY2026 H1 SBC was $386.6M, including $273.6M recognized on IPO-triggered RSU vesting (10-Q). The model uses GAAP EBIT after SBC (SBC 67%/14%/8%/7%/6% of revenue FY26-30) and holds the diluted count flat at 298.4M (which already includes options, RSUs and all contingent warrants) with no buyback offset, so SBC is counted once. Peers' P/E and EV/sales are on consensus (mostly non-GAAP) EPS; EV/sales is unaffected by the SBC basis.

defense_exposure.detail: The filings give no defense, military or intelligence revenue line. Named large customers are commercial or academic: G42 24% and MBZUAI 62% of FY2025 revenue (424B4); in Q2 2026, Customer A 34%, OpenAI ~32% ($56.8M) and a third customer 10% (10-Q). The prospectus lists 'defense organizations' among on-premises customers alongside national laboratories (DOE labs are civilian government under the book's definition). The one disclosed defense award is a $45M DARPA contract shared with Ranovus (April 2025). Even if Cerebras booked half of it evenly over 2-3 years, that is under $15M a year, ~1-2% of FY2026 revenue of ~$885M. The unnamed 10% customer in Q2 2026 cannot be classified from the filings.

reasoning: Evidence (primary documents first). Q2 2026 10-Q and release: core revenue $209.9M (+103% y/y), GAAP revenue $180.1M with cloud 70% of it. GAAP gross margin fell to 14% on next-gen transition charges and new-capacity depreciation; core GM was 40.6%. FY2026 core guide was raised to $880-890M, and the CFO says revenue will 'more than triple' in 2027 (consensus FY2027 $2.95B, 11 analysts). RPO is $25.4B, mostly the OpenAI 750MW committed-capacity MRA: 22% by mid-2028, 43% in months 25-48. Capex was $549M in H1, against $8.6B of liquidity. On fully diluted shares (298.4M incl. 26.1M contingent warrant shares) the stock is ~$44B of equity and ~$37.7B EV: ~12.8x consensus 2027 revenue and ~16x NTM. Valuation: DCF at a 14.8% WACC (comparable beta 2.29, rf 5.24%, ERP 4.20%) with exit 14x FY2030 EBITDA gives $104. 7.0x NTM EV/sales at the horizon, below the 11-peer CY2027 median of 10.0x (justified by neocloud-like capacity economics, low GAAP margins and OpenAI concentration), gives $138. Blend $124.76 = engine base. Scenarios: bear $61 (25%, OpenAI shifts work / ramp slips, neocloud multiple), base $125 (50%), bull $209 (25%, OpenAI expansion option, AWS/AMD channels, ~11x). Distribution: mix of lognormals with sigma ~0.30-0.35 within each scenario. Base rates: 115% realized IPO-period vol (inflated) and the typical first-year drift of large AI IPOs after unlocks. The ladder centres on ~$125 with P(>=149) = 0.36. It sits below spot because, on my cash flows, the current price already discounts multi-year execution. The 11 Strong Buy/Buy ratings and $292 average target are underwriter-heavy and treated as weak evidence. Upside tail kept at 4% for >=$298 and 1.5% for >=$372. Research limits: investors.cerebras.ai and Zacks blocked fetching (403/bot check, not circumvented); no call transcript was reachable; Twelve Data/Alpha Vantage estimate endpoints are premium. Peer EV/EBITDA forward was not available, so the peer test uses EV/sales and P/E. Lane share: 11 of 30 sources are primary documents (10-Q, two results releases, 424B4, closing 8-K, Form 144, 13D/A, XBRL facts, EDGAR index, company newsroom, peer XBRL). That is below the 60% target because the comps rule needs a consensus page for each of 11 peers. Excluding those 13 comp-data pages, 11 of 17 (65%) are primary.
